verdict_reason: Framing review of two measurement designs before implementation; several premises of the sketch (window-share attribution, hook visibility, one outcome vocabulary) are contradicted or untested in the evidence, so the design should be revised before the closed vocabulary is published.
reply_markdown:
**Framing.** The sketch treats the vocabulary as the hard commitment and the score as later work. Invert it: scores will be revised many times, so publish only raw closed measures (with `unknown` for what a host cannot see) and derive every score nightly. Two premises are shaky: (i) window share is not attributable — the 5-hour window moved 8→72 % with no run of ours (state.md 11:57) and 260k tokens moved it 30→65 % (09:02); (ii) usefulness is confounded — hard tasks get high effort, so high effort will look worse. To choose I need: how often accounts have other consumers; whether z.ai has a fourth tier on glm-5.3; what SubagentStop really carries; and the install count (below ~50, per-tier tables stay noise).

**Q1.** gpt-6-astra: chore low, reading/digest **medium** (a cheap digest poisons the judge), checkpoint medium, diff-review high, acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh. glm-5.3: scout low, checkpoint/diff-review/acceptance high, max only for stuck/core-contract or as second judge on disagreement — GLM is the cheap, window-free workhorse; move non-acceptance to it. Express roster policy as **presets or floor/cap**, never endpoint tiers: z.ai maps medium→high and xhigh→max, so "checkpoint medium" is high on GLM; events must carry `effort` (sent) and `effort_requested` (preset) or the table compares incomparable tiers. Denominator: a **vector**, not a scalar — confirmed findings per window-share-point, per money, per wall-minute; score window share only when the run's own delta explains the movement. Unlisted designs: (a) raw-only schema + nightly derived scores (revisable without a break); (b) randomised exploration — 10–20 % of runs one tier off policy, flagged `effort_source: explore`; (c) paired judging — same digest at high and xhigh; disagreement rate is the top tier's marginal value; (d) effort ratchet — escalate only on empty/invalid reply.

**Q2.** SubagentStop is the right *closing* point, but pair it with SubagentStart: a worker dying with the host emits nothing, so error shares are survivorship-biased (next start closes an orphan as `unknown`). The hook sees the **agent definition name**, not model or effort: tier from the name (closed list), model through CLAUDE_MODELS, `effort` + `effort_source: hook|transcript|rate|unknown` — `workers rate --effort` must never silently claim what the hook did not see. Never send: prompts, briefs, paths, transcript/session ids, agent labels as typed (custom names carry customer names → map or `other`), free-text notes, verification pattern names (boolean only). Attribution under rework: a pseudonymous `wave_ref` per wave, per-worker `useful` marks and credited-finding **counts** (no ids); a reworked worker is `partly` by definition and the rework is its own event; `verified` stays the objective signal; wave success is never inferred from worker outcome. Other hosts fit only if `other`/`unknown` is first-class, not a degradation.

**Q3.** Consult: `effort`, `effort_requested`, `effort_source`, `effort_mapping`, `quota_cost` **bucketed** (exact percentages leak account size). Rating: `findings_confirmed` / `findings_implemented` counts at rating time — alternative 3's join without intake-side ids. New `worker` event: host, tier, model, effort, effort_source, duration bucket, outcome class, token/tool/edits buckets, `verified`, `resumes`, `wave_ref`. All optional-with-`unknown`, additive: `close_event` must keep events missing new fields (old clients) and must stop discarding non-consultation|rating types (classes.rs:870). No derived scores, no free text; never reuse the intake's free-text `agent_report`.

**Q4.** Scout-and-judge fails on compression loss and anchoring — a confident wrong digest is worse than none. Caps: (1) digest = **map**, not summary — one line per changed file, no correctness claims; (2) ≤40 lines / 4 KB with machine-checked **coverage** — every diffstat file appears once or the digest is discarded and the judge gets raw; (3) the judge always gets diffstat + file list + ≤N raw-hunk requests (one budgeted call); (4) the judge's cap is in **calls** (1 + ≤2 escalations on empty/invalid replies) — the window is not token-linear; (5) audit arm: 1 in 5 judgings gets the raw diff; the confirmed-finding gap measures digest loss. A blocker claim must quote a raw path:line.

## Requested checks
- **RC1** (finding #2) — cwd: the xelth.com repo. Read `docs/t-hub` and the intake's event parser. Read-only, 30 min. Settles whether unknown `event_type`/details fields are dropped, 400-refused or stored; the worker event's phasing depends on it.
- **RC2** (Q1) — cwd: this repo. One `c3 consult` chore to z.ai glm-5.3 with `--native-effort xhigh`; observe accept/refuse and ledger `effort_confirmed`. Workspace-write (small quota cost), 5 min. Settles the fourth-tier question.
- **RC3** (Q2) — cwd: scratch. SubagentStart/Stop hooks dumping stdin JSON to a temp file; run one Task with a haiku agent and an explicit effort override. Workspace-write, 10 min. Settles whether the payload carries model/effort or only the agent name.
- **RC4** (finding #3) — cwd: this machine. Script over `~/.codex/sessions` rollouts: per-run window deltas vs total window movement. Read-only, 20 min. Settles the attributable share of window consumption.

findings.claim: The two planning sources define different closed worker-outcome vocabularies (handoff: reported|stopped-by-coordinator|error|unknown; state.md: completed|error:rate_limit|error:context|error:other|stopped). A closed vocabulary that ships from contradictory sketches will be wrong for one of them and unchangeable once published.
findings.trigger: Implementing worker telemetry from either document without reconciling the outcome class list.

evidence.observation: outcome class listed as reported | stopped-by-coordinator | error | unknown
outcome listed as completed, error:rate_limit, error:context, error:other, stopped

findings.verification: Grep both documents for the outcome lists and diff them; confirm no third source already picks one.
findings.remedy: Adopt the finer list (completed|stopped|error:rate_limit|error:context|error:other|unknown): error cause is the tier signal; map reported->completed, stopped-by-coordinator->stopped; write it into the schema doc before any code.

findings.claim: The client-side closer rebuilds every event from a fixed key set and discards any event_type other than consultation|rating (close_event returns None). A new worker event, and new fields such as effort on existing events, are silently dropped on old or un-updated code paths unless the closer is extended in the same release with additive semantics (absent new fields must still close).
findings.trigger: Queueing a worker event or an effort-carrying consult event and letting close_event_body run before send.

evidence.observation: if event_type != "consultation" && event_type != "rating" { return None } - the event is discarded
details rebuilt key by key from a fixed allowlist; unknown keys never leave, unknown shapes become other/unknown
Details/RatingDetails structs carry no effort field today

findings.verification: Add a unit test: a worker event closes to itself; a consultation without effort closes unchanged; run cargo test -p c3 telemetry.
findings.remedy: Extend close_event and the constructors with event_type worker and optional effort fields in one release; state explicitly that missing new fields close to absent/unknown so old clients' events keep flowing.

findings.claim: The proposed tier score (usefulness per 5-hour-window share) is not computable from published telemetry (the event carries tokens but no quota cost) and is biased where it is computable: the window moved 8->72 % without our runs (another consumer) and 260k tokens moved it 30->65 % (non-linear), so per-run window share is both unattributable and non-monotone in effort.
findings.trigger: Aggregating usefulness per window share at the intake from current event fields.

evidence.observation: window 8 % -> 72 % between 11:18 and 11:55 WITHOUT our runs; another consumer on the account
window went 30 -> 65 % for 260k tokens inside one round - non-linear
quota cost lives only in the ledger (to_quota); the consult event has tokens_in/out but no window share

findings.verification: RC4: compute per-run window deltas against total window movement on one day of local rollouts and report the attributable fraction.
findings.remedy: Add a bucketed quota_cost to the consult event; score window share only for runs whose delta explains the movement, else mark unscoreable; always publish the token/wall vector so other denominators can be derived later.

findings.claim: Effort tiers are endpoint-local (z.ai: low|high|max with medium->high, xhigh->max; openai: low|medium|high|xhigh). A roster policy written in universal tier names silently overspends on GLM - 'checkpoint medium' is high there - so a per-purpose policy must be expressed in preset names or floor/cap and the SENT tier must be recorded, or the usefulness table compares incomparable tiers.
findings.trigger: Applying the sketch's per-purpose effort policy to glm-5.3 through the caps-v1 mapping.

evidence.observation: z.ai low|high|max with medium->high and xhigh->max; openai low|medium|high|xhigh
caps-v1 rows give api.z.ai the zai vocabulary, builtin:openai the openai vocabulary

findings.verification: Trace one preset (checkpoint -> medium) through the zai mapping and confirm the ledger's effort_sent becomes high.
findings.remedy: Store presets/floor-cap in the roster entry; send effort (post-mapping) and effort_requested (preset) in events; group the usefulness table by sent tier within endpoint vocabulary.

findings.claim: SubagentStop alone yields survivorship-biased and missing-not-at-random data: a worker dying with the host emits no event (error share understated), and the hook carries the agent definition name, not the model or the effort (an explicit Agent-call effort override may be absent from the transcript), so the effort dimension would be systematically empty exactly where it matters.
findings.trigger: Counting tier x effort completion rates from SubagentStop events only.

evidence.observation: hook fires at agent end with the agent id; tier from the plugin's agent names; effort lives in the definition frontmatter; an Agent-call override 'may not be in the subagent transcript - an open question'
model and effort presence in the payload is unverified

findings.verification: RC3: dump the SubagentStart/Stop stdin JSON for one haiku Task with an explicit effort override and inspect which fields exist.
findings.remedy: Pair Start+Stop (orphan Start closed as unknown on next start); record tier, model and effort each with its own source field (hook|transcript|rate|unknown); never let the rate command fill a field the hook did not observe.

findings.claim: The intake already has a free-text agent_report event and the rate command has a --note; the worker event must be a distinct closed class and notes must never leave the machine, or the closed-class contract is broken on the first convenience path.
findings.trigger: Implementing c3 workers rate with a note and reusing the existing intake worker/agent table.

evidence.observation: intake has agent_report with task_scope free text from an older project; 'the worker event must NOT reuse it'

findings.verification: Grep the worker-event plan and rate command for any free-text field destined for the intake.
findings.remedy: New event class worker with closed fields only; --note stored locally beside the mark, never serialised into telemetry.

findings.claim: Scout-and-judge fails by compression loss and anchoring: a confident wrong digest misleads the judge worse than no digest, and nothing in the sketch measures that loss.
findings.trigger: Routing a reading pass (GLM low / Haiku) whose digest omits a defect that the judge then never sees.

evidence.observation: scout writes the digest handoff, the judge gets the digest plus a call cap; no coverage rule or audit arm specified
an observational usefulness table cannot separate digest loss from tier quality without a raw-diff control arm

findings.verification: Run 5 judgings with raw diff and 5 with digest on one wave; compare confirmed findings (a pilot of the audit arm).
findings.remedy: Digest as a per-file map with machine-checked coverage and a size cap; judge gets diffstat + file list + limited raw-hunk requests; 1-in-5 raw-diff audit arm; judge cap in calls, not tokens.

findings.claim: Splitting usefulness per reviewer x effort from observational runs confounds tier quality with task difficulty (hard tasks are sent at high effort), so the table will make the expensive tiers look worse; and any derived score published inside the closed vocabulary freezes a definition that will need revision.
findings.trigger: Aggregating the intake's usefulness table per reviewer x effort after months of policy-driven routing.

evidence.observation: sketch plans a usefulness table split per reviewer x effort and scores a tier by usefulness per window share
effort is chosen from the purpose, so effort correlates with task class by construction

findings.verification: Before trusting the table, check within one purpose whether effort assignment varies at all; if not, no identification is possible.
findings.remedy: Add an exploration flag (10-20 % of runs one tier off policy) and/or paired same-brief judgings; publish only raw counts and let nightly derived scores live outside the schema.

unproven: Whether z.ai exposes more than three reasoning tiers on glm-5.3 (RC2).
What the SubagentStart/Stop hook payload actually contains (model, effort, agent name) on current Claude Code (RC3).
Whether the intake drops, rejects or stores unknown event types and unknown details fields (RC1).
The fraction of 5-hour window movement attributable to a single installation's runs (RC4).
The number of reporting installs needed for a per-tier usefulness table to beat noise.
